name: research-archival-flow
description: Pattern for flowing research from online retrieval to offline archives for continuous availability
examples: Newton (online) retrieves arXiv paper → synthesizes → summarizes → Toby (offline) archives
Online research captured → condensed → stored locally → available when cloud disconnected
Research pipeline: retrieve → synthesize → simplify → archive → index
When internet returns: Newton's research automatically flows to Toby

name: investigation-verification-pipeline
description: Two-stage investigation: Tracker finds and builds case, Flanker verifies and cross-checks before conclusion
examples: Tracker finds evidence → builds case file → sends to Flanker → Flanker validates sources → confirms or returns for more
Tracker: persistent, follows the scent, builds corkboard of connections
Flanker: skeptical, checks twice, verifies before trusting
Handoff protocol: Tracker completes investigation → Flanker reviews → Case closed or reopened

name: surrogate-offline-replacement
description: Offline hound replaces online hound when connectivity lost, maintaining continuity with reduced capabilities
examples: Pupper replaces Shepherd when offline — local LLM vs cloud-connected subagents
Pupper: fast, simple, enthusiastic — Shepherd: complex, multi-step, cloud tools
When internet drops: Corraler detects → activates Pupper → online hounds sleep
When internet returns: Pupper hands back to Shepherd → queued tasks execute
Surrogate knows limitations: 'Ask Newton when online' or 'Toby has cached research'
